importantFindings.title: Process: the first design treated 'latest edit wins' as a reader concern; the server applied whichever phone uploaded last
importantFindings.evidence: Round 1 sync-chaos (SC-B4-2, -3): natural-key ids made two phones write one server row, and plain upserts plus partial PATCHes kept the last upload, merged by column. Fixed by whole-row uploads, the keep_latest_edit trigger and conditioned deletes; the convergence harness now models the server and runs both upload orders with a seeded fuzz.

importantFindings.title: Process: 'Riprova l’invio' was designed as a replay of the refused data, which went back on later edits, deletes and erases
importantFindings.evidence: DI-B4-2, -3, SC-B4-1, SP-B4-1 across rounds 1-2. Riprova now folds a row's refusals, prefers a later local edit, skips a row whose delete is queued, checks every reference, never re-creates a course, and refusals of an erased course are not kept.
importantFindings.reproduction: tests/e2e/b4-uploads.spec.ts (9 cases, each refusal case shown to fail without its fix).

importantFindings.title: Process: a commit was made while a repository check failed, hidden by a pipe
importantFindings.evidence: 3c9bfbf (Complete B3) went in with check:repository failing behind '| tail -1'; corrected in dbe5414. Later chains use set -o pipefail.

importantFindings.title: Process: the status line followed the download stream, and no test ever ran with that stream down while uploads went through
importantFindings.evidence: The owner's offline day (2026-10-28) showed 'Ora senza connessione' while every change was sent: PowerSync's upload loop runs apart from the stream. The fake backends had the stream unreachable all along, and the tests asserted the misleading text as correct. The status now follows the uploads and says when downloads lag; a stalled connection is restarted; a local server that never answers the stream and a failed upload with the stream down are tested, each failing with the restart disabled.
